title: Endomorphisms of the ring complex are self-dual under evaluation
statement: For a small site (C,J) and a sheaf R of commutative rings, let U=R[0] be the ring complex and e:Hom(U,U)≅U the evaluation-at-one isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-completion-unit], with the actual internal Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex]. For every endomorphism a:U→U, contravariant Hom(a,U) followed by e.hom equals e.hom followed by a. No nonzero hypothesis on R or nonempty hypothesis on the site is imposed.

source.place: Section 0A8X, section-hom-complexes; sites-modules.tex, internal Hom and evaluation on the coefficient ring module

proof.text: For endomorphisms f and g of the coefficient ring module, linearity gives f(x)=x*f(1) and g(x)=x*g(1). Commutativity gives f(g(1))=g(f(1)). Apply this identity sectionwise to a local internal-Hom section and the given sheaf endomorphism. Extensionality identifies precomposition followed by evaluation at one with evaluation at one followed by that endomorphism.

For an object isomorphic to the coefficient ring module, conjugate the endomorphism across that isomorphism. Use internal-Hom composition and evaluation naturality to transport the preceding identity.

For the ring complex, use its degree-zero identification with the coefficient ring module. Apply the Hom-complex map projection formula in source and target degree zero, followed by the transported identity. In every other degree the target ring-complex term is a zero object, so the two component maps are equal. Componentwise extensionality completes the proof.

theorem ringComplexEndomorphism_selfDual
    {C : Type v} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{v})
    (a : ringedSiteRingComplex R ⟶ ringedSiteRingComplex R) :
    ((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).flip.obj (ringedSiteRingComplex R)).map a.op ≫
        (ringedHomUnitEvaluationIso R (ringedSiteRingComplex R)).hom =
      (ringedHomUnitEvaluationIso R (ringedSiteRingComplex R)).hom ≫ a
